record.paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
record.original_question: Given a finite pattern p and an integer k, is it decidable whether p is k-avoidable, meaning whether there exists an infinite word over a k-letter alphabet that avoids p?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A pattern is a finite nonempty word p over an alphabet of variables. An infinite word w over a finite alphabet A is said to avoid p if there is no nonerasing morphism h from the free monoid on the variables of p to A* such that h(p) occurs as a factor of w. For an integer k ≥ 1, the pattern p is called k-avoidable if there exists an infinite word over some k-letter alphabet that avoids p; otherwise p is called k-unavoidable. The avoidability index of p is the smallest k for which p is k-avoidable (and ∞ if no such k exists).

Question: Is the following decision problem decidable? Given as input a finite pattern p (over a finite set of variables) and a positive integer k, determine whether p is k-avoidable.

Equivalently, does there exist an algorithm that, given (p, k), computes whether the avoidability index of p is at most k?
artifact.status_search_result: While Bean–Ehrenfeucht–McNulty and Zimin gave an algorithm deciding whether a pattern is avoidable at all (i.e., k-avoidable for some k), no algorithm is known to decide, for given k and p, whether p is k-avoidable; computing the avoidability index of a pattern remains a long-standing open problem in combinatorics on words. Even individual short patterns (e.g., αα ββ γγ) have unresolved avoidability indices.

status_evidence.title: Survey of combinatorics on words and patterns
status_evidence.snippet: There is no known algorithm to compute the avoidability index of a given pattern; even for short patterns the exact value may be unknown.
status_evidence.claim: Deciding the avoidability index (equivalently k-avoidability) of a pattern is an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Outstanding Challenges in Combinatorics on Words (BIRS 12w5068)
status_evidence.snippet: Computing the avoidability index of a pattern is listed among outstanding open challenges.
status_evidence.claim: The k-avoidability decision problem is still considered open in the community.
